issues.legal_issue: A court admitting an insufficiently stamped instrument in evidence has no discretion to impose less than the fixed statutory penalty when the higher-penalty trigger applies.
material_facts: The instruments tendered in civil suits were found to be insufficiently stamped and were impounded.
The trial court admitted the instruments in evidence after requiring the deficit duty and a penalty twice the deficit duty.
The High Court held that the penalty had to be ten times the deficit duty.
issues.conclusion: Under Sections 33 and 34 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, the court admitting an insufficiently stamped instrument must impose the prescribed tenfold penalty when the statutory trigger for that penalty is met; it has no discretion to reduce it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 33 requires an authority receiving evidence to impound an instrument that appears insufficiently stamped. Section 34 makes such an instrument inadmissible unless the duty and prescribed penalty are paid, and fixes the higher penalty where its statutory trigger applies. Unlike Section 34, Section 39 expressly gives the Deputy Commissioner discretion to impose a lesser penalty, while Section 38 permits the Deputy Commissioner to refund part of a penalty. The Court upheld the interpretation of Sections 33 and 34 in Digambar Warty v. District Registrar, Bangalore Urban District, and another.

rule.if: civil_evidence_admission_proceeding and instrument_insufficiently_stamped and court_admits_instrument_as_evidence and higher_fixed_penalty_trigger_met

predicates.civil_evidence_admission_proceeding: The proceeding involves a court deciding whether to admit an instrument in evidence in a civil case.
predicates.instrument_insufficiently_stamped: The instrument tendered in evidence bears less stamp duty than is required.
predicates.court_admits_instrument_as_evidence: The court admits the instrument in evidence after addressing its insufficient stamping.
predicates.higher_fixed_penalty_trigger_met: The facts satisfy the statutory condition for the higher fixed penalty rather than the lower minimum penalty.

issues.definition: When a court admits an insufficiently stamped instrument in a civil evidence proceeding and the higher fixed-penalty condition is met, the required output is a tenfold penalty.

issues.legal_issue: A reduced penalty may be confirmed and the penalty dispute closed in the particular circumstances where requiring payment of the full penalty followed by a refund application would prolong an already delayed matter and the reduction rested on mitigating circumstances.
material_facts: The trial court reduced the penalty because the plaintiffs were agricultural workers and the agreements had been prepared by local villagers whom the court considered inexperienced in document preparation.
The trial court considered the full penalty harsh in light of those circumstances.
The penalty order had been made more than five years before the Supreme Court considered the appeal.
Requiring payment of the full penalty followed by an application to the Deputy Commissioner for a refund would entail further proceedings.
Section 38 empowered the Deputy Commissioner to refund part of a penalty.
issues.conclusion: In the circumstances of this case, the Court confirmed the trial court's direction to pay the deficit duty and a penalty twice that duty, and closed the penalty proceedings rather than requiring payment of the full penalty followed by a refund application.
issues.legal_principle: Although Sections 33 and 34 require the court admitting an insufficiently stamped instrument to impose the prescribed penalty, Section 38 gives the Deputy Commissioner power to refund part of a penalty. Given the trial court's mitigating reasons and the delay and further proceedings that the refund route would involve, the Court resolved this appeal by confirming the reduced penalty. This case-specific disposition did not alter the Court's interpretation of Sections 33 and 34.

predicates.appeal_concerning_stamp_penalty: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the penalty imposed for an insufficiently stamped instrument.
predicates.lower_court_found_mitigating_circumstanc: The lower court relied on circumstances such as the parties' limited experience with document preparation in reducing the penalty.
predicates.penalty_dispute_already_delayed: The penalty dispute had remained unresolved for a substantial time before appellate consideration.
predicates.full_payment_then_refund_would_prolong_p: Requiring payment of the full penalty and a later application for a refund would require further proceedings and delay resolution.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning a stamp penalty involves mitigating circumstances, an already delayed dispute, and a refund route that would prolong proceedings, the output is confirmation of the reduced penalty and closure of the penalty dispute.
